description: The canonical spec-driven scaffold Airrow generates for a new customer project — the single source of truth for generated output. The app enumerates template/** (excluding this file), substitutes {{TOKENS}} with values derived from the interview, and writes the result only after the founder approves the preview.

tokens.DOMAIN_OVERVIEW: What is built, for whom, and the core value.
tokens.VISION: Long-term vision — what this becomes if it wins.
tokens.MVP_FOCUS: What the MVP must do above all else.
tokens.CAPABILITY_SCOPE: Bullet list of the capabilities selected for v1.
tokens.CAPABILITY_SPECS: One section per selected capability: what to spec and what it must cover.
tokens.TENANCY_MODEL: How data is organized and isolated between users/organizations.
tokens.AUTH_MODEL: How users sign in, and what that implies for the data layer.
tokens.ROLES: User types and what each may do.
tokens.CORE_ENTITIES: The 3-7 most important objects and their relationships.
tokens.INTEGRATIONS: External systems this product integrates with.
tokens.SECURITY_POSTURE: Encryption, audit, and privacy posture from the data-sensitivity answer.
tokens.SCALE_POSTURE: Caching, database, and performance posture for the v1 scale target.
tokens.STACK_SUMMARY: One-line description of the technical stack.
tokens.STACK_DETAIL: Fuller stack description, naming the database/backend accurately.
tokens.REPO_PROVIDER: Where the code lives (GitHub / Azure DevOps).
tokens.SETUP_STEPS: Ordered steps that need a human with an account — everything /start deliberately does not do.
tokens.START_BOOTSTRAP: Framework-specific scaffold + toolchain steps that /start runs.
tokens.START_MINIMUM: What the bare minimum that runs means for this project — and, as firmly, what it does not.
tokens.FIRST_SPEC_HINT: What to write the first spec for, derived from the MVP focus.
tokens.CMD_DEV: Command to start the dev server.
tokens.ARCHITECTURE_INVARIANTS: Constitution I — data-flow direction, where external calls happen, error/return patterns, autogenerated files.
tokens.DATA_INVARIANTS: Constitution II — data model rules, access control, migration rules.
tokens.DESIGN_INVARIANTS: Constitution III — design tokens, component reuse.
tokens.ARCHITECTURE_LAYERS: Prose description of the layers and one-way data flow.
tokens.ISSUE_TERM: What a unit of work is called (issue / work item).
tokens.BOARD_TERM: What groups issues into a feature (GitHub Project / Azure Boards area path).
tokens.CI_FILE: Path of this project's CI definition.
tokens.DEPLOY_FILE: Path of this project's DEV deploy definition.
tokens.SECRETS_HOME: Where CI credentials live, named as the provider names them.
tokens.CLI_NAME: The provider CLI the founder needs installed.
tokens.CLI_ISSUE_VIEW: Command that reads one issue / work item.
tokens.CLI_BRANCH_LINK: Command(s) that create the issue branch and link it to the tracker.
tokens.CLI_PR_CREATE: Command that opens a pull request.
tokens.CI_SETUP_STEPS_AZ: Azure Pipelines steps (indented) that set up the toolchain.
tokens.CI_READY_CHECK_AZ: Azure Pipelines shell (indented) deciding whether /start has run.
tokens.CI_SETUP_STEPS: YAML steps (indented) that set up the toolchain in CI.
tokens.CI_READY_CHECK: Shell (indented) deciding whether /start has run, so CI does not go red on an empty repo.
tokens.DEPLOY_STEPS: YAML steps (indented) that deploy to DEV using ${{ secrets.* }}.
